title: Early access needs peak standards applied
full_text:
A sector specialist has recommended trustees satisfy the more onerous requirements the Income Tax Assessment Act (ITAA) stipulates when looking to access superannuation benefits early using the permanent incapacity condition of release in all circumstances.
Accurium head of SMSF education Mark Ellem made the suggestion recognising the difference between the relevant rules set out in the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) (SIS) Regulations and the ITAA regarding the matter.
To this end, to use the permanent incapacity condition of release under SIS Regulation 1.03C requires the fund trustees be reasonably satisfied the member’s ill-health, whether physical or mental, makes it unlikely the member will engage in gainful employment for which they are reasonably qualified by education, training or experience.
However, the ITAA imposes a more burdensome threshold to be satisfied in order to receive the tax concessions associated with a permanent incapacity condition of release. Under Section 995.1 of this legislation, the benefit has been paid to an individual because they suffer from ill-health, whether physical or mental, and two legally qualified medical practitioners have certified that because of the ill-health, it is unlikely the individual can ever be gainfully employed in a capacity for which they are reasonably qualified because of education, experience or training.
“So if I want the tax concessions, I need to get the two certificates. [But] I would say you’ll need to get the two certificates anyway,” Ellem told delegates at The Tax Institute National Superannuation Conference held in Melbourne last week.
“[This is] because [of who] the trustees will have to [convince] they have legally accessed [their superannuation benefits] under the permanent incapacity condition of release. They are the auditor and possibly the ATO.
“Do you think the trustee’s decision that ‘yeah, I satisfy a permanent incapacity [definition]’ is sufficient appropriate audit evidence? What do you think they are going to want?
“They’ll probably want you to go to the extent of the tax definition to substantiate that you could [legally] access [your superannuation savings using this condition of release].”
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation and Investments
